public_sources: Mirea et al. 2024 persistent latent-cause inference
Adams and MacKay 2007 Bayesian online changepoint detection
Shappell et al. 2019 hidden semi-Markov brain-state modeling

actions: Replaced the coarse sticky-HMM engineering screen with a direct predictive run-length/persistence control plus a multivariate unlabeled covariance/subspace-change likelihood.
Fit the observation-change GMM without switch/silence labels on disjoint mixed calibration streams; locked hazard and detector thresholds before held-out normal/strong rank-collapse tests.
Evaluated detector discrimination, false silence alarms, latency, Brier score and ECE across PAST/GROUSE-like and Oja-like trackers under altered switch/silence hazards.
Used the unsupervised global-change and temporary-silence cause likelihoods for dormant-memory release and admission on separate delayed/sparse-feedback held-out streams.
Persisted and read back the delta and advanced LATEST. No aggregate ledger, other-role state, O state, downstream state, or legacy research was read.
result: Substantive bounded update. The five-feature unlabeled cause likelihood is useful for separating global context changes from temporary latent silences and sharply reduces memory churn/stale harm. A single fixed-hazard run-length persistence prior does not improve that detector and degrades strong-rank-collapse detection/calibration. Cause-specific admission is too conservative to establish an overall task-loss gain.
blocker: Source-exact SPLiT S1 Code.zip remains unavailable through the current read-only public transport; the run did not mutate or probe external state to obtain it.
termination: runtime checkpoint with nonempty frontier; no global completion claim
exact_next_action: Continue read-only SPLiT S1 Code.zip recovery. Replace the single geometric persistence/run-length process with an explicit-duration hierarchical latent-state model separating temporary silence from persistent context change, and add utility-aware expected-benefit versus stale-cost admission. Calibrate on disjoint streams, lock parameters, and compare against the currently stronger unsupervised GMM-only detector under altered hazards and both tracker/feedback families.
